name: Reel
text: We should assign a dedicated person to focus on unresolved blockers, because this will help us remove obstacles quickly and make progress toward our goal of 100% link coverage. By doing this, we accept the trade-off of taking a team member away from other tasks, but it's worth it because it will help us move faster in the long run. Having someone solely focused on blockers will ensure they get the attention they need and we can avoid delays. This is a better option than trying to handle blockers as a side task, which can lead to slow progress and decreased quality.

name: Scriv
text: Assigning a dedicated person to focus on unresolved blockers may not be the best approach, as it could lead to a single point of failure and create a bottleneck if that person is unavailable. A better alternative might be to implement a rotating ownership model, where multiple team members take turns addressing blockers, to distribute the responsibility and ensure progress continues even if one person is absent. To settle the argument, we need to weigh the potential benefits of dedicated focus against the risks of relying on a single person and consider the impact on the team's overall workload and productivity.
